name: Tamarind Rush
description: Tamarind Rush is a tangy, aggressively carbonated synth-tamarind soda with a chili-salt rim-powder sold separately in a small packet attached to every can. It dominates Tier 1-3 markets and has a cult following among working-class augmentation crews who call it 'the shift drink.'
flavor_profile: Sharp sour-sweet tamarind, a slow-building mild chili heat at the back of the throat, with a salted finish that makes the next sip immediately necessary
cultural_context: Tamarind Rush is the unofficial drink of Meridian 88's labor class. Maintenance crews, chrome-shop apprentices, and transit workers keep a can in every pocket. The chili-salt packet ritual — wetting the can rim, pouring the powder, letting it dissolve — is a small, shared ceremony of the working shift. Mid-tier food reviewers who 'discover' it are mocked for their surprise.
story_hooks: Vexa has quietly reformulated the synth-tamarind base to cut costs, and longtime drinkers can taste the difference; a grassroots boycott is organizing on underground mesh-nets.
The chili-salt packets have a batch number that, when decoded, maps to a hidden drop-point network used by a labor-rights courier cell.

A Tier 4 corponation executive has developed a genuine dependency on Tamarind Rush's specific flavor profile after a Shelf childhood — and is desperately trying to keep this fact hidden from her board.
